summary_paragraph: Mrs. ___ was admitted for persistent nausea, vomiting, and poor oral intake following radiation therapy for tracheal cancer, which led to dehydration, metabolic acidosis, and new-onset atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular rate. She was initially managed in the ICU with IV diltiazem for rate control, which was later transitioned to oral metoprolol after spontaneous conversion to sinus rhythm. Her acidosis, likely due to starvation ketoacidosis, resolved with fluid resuscitation and initiation of TPN. Esophagitis, possibly candidal, was treated with fluconazole and a numbing mouthwash. A malpositioned port was identified and replaced to ensure proper delivery of ongoing cancer therapy. She completed her final radiation treatment during admission and showed improvement in oral intake, nutritional status, and overall strength. She was discharged home with services on a revised medication regimen, including metoprolol succinate, continued pain and nausea management, and instructions for wound and nutrition care.
